ADMINISTRATOR OF STOOL LANDS FOR THE YEAR 2024 

INTRODUCTION 

The Committee on Lands and Natural Resources considered the Annual Statement by the 

Audit Committee of the Office of the Administrator of Stool Lands covering the period 

January to December 2024. The Committee met to review the findings, assess the level o
f 

compliance with audit recommendations, and deliberate on key issues that emerged from
 

the report presented by the Audit Commitiee. 

The consideration forms part of the oversight mandate of the Committee in ensuring sound 

financial management, adherence to audit standards and accountability in the operati
ons of 

the Office of the Administrator of Stool Lands in pursuant of Order 240 of the Standing 

Orders of Parliament. 

The Deputy Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, officials from the Ministry of
 Lands 

and Natural Resources as well as officials from the Office of the Administrator of School 

Lands attended upon the Committee during the consideration of the Annual 
Statement by 

the Audit Committee of the Office of the Administrator of Stool Lands for the Year 2024.

BACKGROUND 

The Office of the Administrator of Stool Lands is mandated to mana
ge public lands, 

optimize revenue from land assets, and ensure proper stewardship of l
and resources in 

accordance with national laws and regulations. 

The Public Financial Management Act, 2016 (Act 921) provides, amongst others, t
hat the 

Audit Committee ensures that the covered entity to which it relates ensures the

implementation of recommendations contained in the Internal Audit Report, External 

Audit Report, Parliament’s decision on the Auditor-General’s Report, and the Auditor- 

General’s Management Letter. This Annual Statement by the Audit Committee of the 

Office of the Administrator of Stool Lands for the Year 2024 was therefore submitted in 

compliance with the provisions of the Public Financial Management Act, 2016 (Act 921). 

AUDIT OBJECTIVES AND SCOPE 

The audit sought to evaluate: 

. The validity and completeness of payroll and staff validation systems. 

. Timeliness and accuracy of withholding tax payments, 

. Asset management practices, including tagging and accounting for fixed assets. 

. Revenue collection and bank remittances. 

. Measures to prevent encroachment and ensure proper land use. 

. Operational challenges and mitigation measures. 

Internal Control 

The Audit Committee advised management on the following to improve Internal Controls: 

i Supervision of Revenue Collectors to reduce financial shortages in the Districts and 

Regional Offices. 

ii. Frequent audit to be conducted at revenue shortage Districts and Regional Offices. 

iid. Development of draft Risk Register and Policy for OASL. 

iv. The Accounts Directorate should also embark on financial monitoring exercise. 

Consideration of the Audit Statement 

The Audit Committee presented the major findings of the 2024 Audit Statement and the 

actions taken by management to address them, The following are the key issues considered 

" by the Committee. 

Validation of Officers 

The Audit Commitiee reported that some officers were not validated by the Office of the 

Administrator of Stool Lands due to delays in enrolling their details on the electronic 

payment voucher system of the Controller and Accountant-General. The Committee 

recommended that the Principal Spending Officer and the Head of Human Resource ensure 

that all affected officers are immediately validated to regularise their payroll status. This 

recommendation was fully implemented. The affocted officers have been placed on the 

appropriate payrolls and redeployed accordingly.

Withholding Taxes 

Delays were recorded in the payment of withholding taxes amounting to thirty-two 

thousand eight hundred and six Ghana cedis. The Audit Committee advised management 

{0 ensure the payment of all outstanding amounts to the Ghana Revenue Authority and to 

strengthen internal controls to prevent a recurrence. Management confirmed that the entire 

amount has been paid and that the necessary receipts have been verified by the Internal 

Audit Unit. 

Non-Embossment of Fixed Assets 

The report revealed that some fixed assets were not embossed and recorded properly. The 

Audit Commitiee directed that all assets be tagged with unique identification numbers to 

enhance tracking and accountability. 

The Committee noted that this directive has been complied with as all assets have been 

embossed and inventoried by the Estate Unit. 

Unaccounted Revenue 

An amount of Seven Thousand, Seven Hundred and Forty Ghana Cedis (GHS7,740) was 

reported as unaccounted for. The Audit Committce instructed that the amount be recovered 

and paid into the designated bank account of the Office of the Administrator of Stool Lands. 

The Commitice was informed that the entire amount has been recovered from the 

responsible officers and deposited into the official account. 

Encroachment on Lands 

The report indicated instances of encroachment on lands belonging to the Office of the 

Administrator of Stool Lands in the Northern Region. The Audit Committee recommended 

the fencing of the affected lands and the development of a comprehensive land 

" management plan to prevent further encroachment. Management informed the Committee 

that funds have been carmarked in the 2025 budget and procurement plan has been made 

for the construction of a perimeter wall. 

Absence of Designated Driver in the Upper East Region 

The absence of a designated driver in the Upper East Region created operational 

challenges. The Audit Committec recommended that temporary arrangements be made to 

ensure mobility for official duties. The Committee was informed that a driver has been 

assigned to the region through the Regional Coordinating Council.

Unearned Salaries 

The Committee examined instances of unearned salaries in the Ashanti, Bono, and 

Northern Regions. It was established that an officer had travelled outside the country while 

still on the payroll. Management confirmed that the unearned salaries have been recovered 

and evidence of repayment submitted to the Audit Unit. 

Control of Revenue Collection 

The Committee expressed concern about delays in banking revenue and weak internal 

control measures. Management explained that officers in remote areas faced challenges 

accessing banking facilities, hence delays occurred. To address this, a mobile money 

payment system has been introduced to facilitate timely transfers into the main account of 

the Office. 

Tt was reported that with the support of the Audit Committee, management implemented 

the audit recommendation which lead to the reirieval of a total amount of Sixty-One 

Thousand, Three Hundred and Ninety Ghana Cedis (GHg¢61,390.00) being IGF collected 

which hitherto was not banked and therefore not accounted for. Details are as follows:

Delayed Budget Releases 

The Committee noted with concern that the Office of the Administrator of Stool Lands had 

. received only *wo months of releases from the Minerals Development Fund, with seven 

months in arrears. Management stated that correspondence has been initiated with the Fund 

and the Ministry of Finance to ensure the immediate release of the outstanding amounts. 

Observations and Recommendations 

The Committee on Lands and Natural Resources observed that management of the Office 

of the Administrator of Stool Lands has made significant progress in implementing the 

recommendations contained in the 2024 Audit Statement. The payment of outstanding 

withholding taxes and the tagging of fixed assets have been completed in accordance with 

the directives of the Audit Committee.

The Committee further noted that certain weaknesses still exist in the internal control 

systems, particularly in the area of revenue collection and reconciliation of Duplicate 

Carbon Receipts. It was recommended that management should strengthen oversight and 

ensure that no new receipt books are issued until previous ones have been fully accounted 

for and certified. 

The Committee expressed concern about the continued encroachment of lands under the 

cate of the Office of the Administrator of Stool Lands. The Committee advised that 

immediate protective measures such as tree planting, the erection of temporary fencing, 

and the placement of site attendants should be considered as cost-effective options pending 

the construction of permanent fence walls. 

In relation to revenue mobilisation, the Committee commended management for 

introducing the mobile money initiative to improve the timeliness of banking, particularly 

in remote areas where access to financial institutions remain limited. Tt was recommended 

that this initiative be fully implemented and closely monitored to prevent revenue leakages 

and enhance accountability. 

The Committee also observed that delays in the release of funds from the Minerals 

Development Fund continue to affect the operations of the Office. Members of the 

Commitice on Lands and Natural Resources urged the Ministry of Lands and Natural
 

Resources to engage the relevant authorities to facilitate timely disbursement of mineral
 

royalty funds to support effective implementation of programmes and projects by 

beneficiary agencies. 

On the issue of missing Duplicate Carbon Receipts, the Committee acknowledged the steps
 

taken by management to report the maiter to the Police and the Economic and Organised
 

Crime Office for investigation. T was recommended that stricter measures be enforced to
 

ensure full accountability by officers responsible for the custody and issuance of
 receipt 

books. 

Finally, the Committee emphasised the need to uphold Article 267 of the Const
itution 

which assigns the collection and management of stool land revenues and royalties
 to the 

Office of the Administrator of Stool Lands. Tt was observed that strict adherence to. this 

constitutional provision would enhance the financial independence of the Office
 of the 

Administrator of Stoo! Lands and ensure that funds are disbursed to the rightful 

beneficiaries without undue delay.

7.0  CONCLUSION 

The Committee recognizes the efforts made by the Office of the Administrator of School 

Lands in addressing previous irregularities and improving internal controls. However, 

persistent challenges around funding delays, encroachments, and operational constraints 

require ongoing attention. 

The Committee recommends that Parliament adopt this report and support necessary 

reforms and funding to strengthen land administration and safeguard national land 

resources effectively.
